content: Pre-training for NLP. The use of pre-training for natural language tasks has been growing in popularity after recent breakthroughs demonstrating improved performance on a wide array of benchmark tasks BIBREF53, BIBREF54. Existing work has generally used a language modeling objective as the pre-training objective; examples include next-word prediction BIBREF55, sentence autoencoding, BIBREF56, and machine translation BIBREF57. BERT BIBREF58 introduces a variation on this in which the goal is to predict the next sentence in a document given the current sentence. Our pre-training objective is similar in spirit, but operates at a conversation level, rather than a document level. We hence view our objective as conversational modeling rather than (only) language modeling. Furthermore, while BERT's sentence prediction objective is framed as a multiple-choice task, our objective is framed as a generative task.
